text.p: A firm dollar and the impact of quality selling kept the gold market on the defensive on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The selling looks like it could be from a producer or an institution. But it surprising to see it at these levels,' a dealer said.
Selling was evident at around $353.35 in early European, late Asian trading, the dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $353.40 per ounce compared with $353.10 on Monday and a close of $353.40/$353.90.
The strong dollar was a major influence in a New York market subdued by Monday's Martin Luther King Day holiday.
That continued into the Far East markets which came under presure from follow-through selling from New York and what some dealers said were Australian producer sales.
The feeling in the market was that the downside would be tested in the near future.
"The dollar has been playing a big part and could take us lower either today or tomorrow (Wednesday)," one dealer said.
He noted that the market had been as low as $351.10/$351.40 but had held around $352.00 overnight while running into selling at $354.00.
"That is getting into a very narrow range. We are so close to $350.00, that we may have to go down and look at it even although the price bounces again very quickly," he said.
However he added there was also the chance of a "wash out" taking the price lower than that.
Platinum was fixed at a fresh low since October 5, 1993 of $356.25, down from the previous low struck on January 8.
"Platinum is suffering due to the stronger dollar and the slumping Japanese stock market," a dealer said.
It was indicated at $356.00/$357.00, down $2.50 from Monday's close.
Palladium took some support from the continuing lack of dialogue between Russian exports and Japanese imports of the metal on 1997 delivery contracts.
It was 10 cents up on the close at $121.00/$122.00 while silver, influenced by uncertain gold prices, was unchanged at $4.72/$4.74.
